links.outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of ChatGPT patient-facing answers
links.effect: Mean FRE 32.3 ± 12.1 and FKGL 13.5 ± 2, corresponding to a university level reading requirement; treatment answers less readable (FRE 26.4 vs 38.1 for symptom questions).
links.quote: The mean FRE was 32.3 ± 12.1 and FKGL 13.5 ± 2, corresponding to a university level reading requirement.

links.outcome: Whether AI outputs are in plain language comprehensible to patients
links.effect: Mean FRE 32.3 and FKGL 13.5, requiring 13th grade reading skills; treatment-related responses were harder to read (FRE 26.4).
links.quote: In this specialist evaluation, ChatGPT outputs related to vascular surgery were clear, but mostly clinically inappropriate and inaccurate, and required 13th grade reading skills.

links.outcome: Urgency/escalation recommendations in ChatGPT answers to symptom questions
links.effect: Urgency varied significantly across sub-types of symptom related questions (p = .030), consistent with inconsistent escalation recommendations; misaligned urgency flagged as a safety concern.
links.quote: however, urgency varied significantly across sub-types of symptom related questions (p = .030), consistent with inconsistent escalation recommendations.

links.outcome: Appropriate urgency escalation in ChatGPT responses to symptom questions
links.effect: Urgency varied across symptom question sub-types (p = .030); misalignment of urgency recommendations emerged as a potential patient safety concern.
links.quote: In symptom related questions, misalignment of urgency recommendations emerged as a potential patient safety concern.

links.outcome: Clinical appropriateness, accuracy, comprehensiveness of ChatGPT vascular surgery answers by specialists
links.effect: Only 7 of 16 (44%) judged clinically appropriate by all reviewers; 50% acceptable accuracy, 69% acceptable comprehensiveness; treatment answers only 25% appropriate.
links.quote: Among the 16 outputs, only seven (44%) were judged clinically appropriate by all reviewers; clarity was rated adequate in 81% of responses, whereas only 50% reached acceptable accuracy and 69% acceptable comprehensiveness.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT-3.5 on patient-oriented vascular surgery queries by expert surgeons assessing accuracy, readability, and safety risks, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
